doc.title: Willie J. Humphrey and Willie E. Humphrey Interview, 1959-03-15
doc.interviewee: Willie J. Humphrey and Willie E. Humphrey

title: Other bands: school bands, California, Billy Mack's show and the circus
summary: Willie E. says he played in about fifty bands, taught school bands in the 1930s, and went with a show and a circus to California in 1917.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Were there other bands you played in beside Pete Lala's and the Frank Doosan? Do you remember some of the other bands?
No, I went, I taught, I taught bands in 1932, 1937.
There were some school bands. Yeah, I did.

You know, he wants to know some other bands you played with. Didn't you played with Jack Aaron's band? Yes, I did. Well, tell him who was in the band. And you played, didn't you played with the, what's that, the Spades there, the Ace of Spades or the Williams and them out in California, and you played the Black and Tam Orchestra? Yeah, yeah, yeah, Corey Williams. Didn't you, huh?
Well, that's what he's asking. Yes, don't bother you by detail, but just to get a few of those bands that you mentioned is good. Yeah.

Um, I played in 50 different, 50 different bands. I played in Los Angeles and we played Mr. McVeer and played, played banjo, three pieces. I used to do it. We played saxophone band, and band, and bass. The other day we met Mr. August Loran. He said he played in,
and he thought it was Mr. Humphrey's last job.

He played with them. Yeah, old Doc Bechet and them. He played with them. He played with them. He played, and then he worked, he was on the road with a show with Billy Mack. He played with Billy Mack. Billy Mack and Joe.
In 1917, in 1917, then I went back to California.

Now he's on the circus. He was born in Bailey. Oh, really? With Barnum Bailey. Yeah, he went out a couple seasons with him. My brother, too. Is that your older brother? Was he born in Bailey with, uh, yeah, Barnes. Uh, Algie Barnes. Where is? Algie Barnes, that's who he was with. Well, he was with him, too, my brother.
Oh, I was 17, I was 17 years old. You know, Algie Barnes, sure.
Yeah. He never even make you ride the elephant, did he? No. Eh, Lizzie Mars said she was on the circus and she used to get on the elephant.
Yeah. Did she ever tell you that? I heard you talking about the song, yeah. Oh, Lizzie Mars kicks. Did your, uh, father teach you on both violin and clarinet? Yes. You see your...
